title: Small Words, Big Impact: 'Bismillah' and 'Alhamdulillah' in Your Child's Day
summary:
Imagine your little one running towards you, eyes gleaming with hunger, asking for their favorite food. As you hand them the plate, you say in a gentle, playful voice, "Bismillah." They imitate you with a smile, then begin to eat. After they finish, you notice them sneeze, so you gently tell them, "Say Alhamdulillah," and they look at you with curiosity. These simple daily moments are true treasures; they are golden opportunities to plant the seeds of remembrance in their little heart, to grow with them and become an integral part of their life.

Children aged two and three learn through imitation and repetition more than anything else. They absorb everything they see and hear around them and spontaneously imitate adults. When we link words of remembrance to specific daily actions—such as saying "Bismillah" before eating, and "Alhamdulillah" after it or when sneezing—we build strong mental connections for them. These words are not just sounds; they are small keys that accustom them to connecting food and blessings to Allah in a simple way that suits their age.

Don't expect them to understand the full meaning at first; what's important is gentle repetition and the love that envelops these words. Be a good role model, and repeat these remembrances in front of them with a clear, joyful voice, without pressure or coercion. With gentle repetition, your child may begin to say them on their own. And these good habits that we instill in them while they are young are a good step that helps your child grow up remembering Allah and feeling grateful, by Allah's will.
try_this: Tonight: Before your child begins to eat their dinner, say "Bismillah" in a clear, joyful voice, and gently encourage them to say it with you before they start eating.
